clue.text: Smack joint next to Kent town

parts.note: the knuckle is a finger joint
Sandwich is a historic town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A slap on the knuckles somewhere near a quaint English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Sandwich is one of its old Cinque Ports.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle sandwich is slang for a punch in the mouth, so a smack in the face.

clue.text: Dark gangster comes after king for award

indicators.note: the dark-and-gangster pair is placed behind the letter for king

parts.note: night is darkness, used here as a noun
a hood is slang for a hoodlum or gangster

explanation.surface: A shady mobster follows the monarch to collect an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A knighthood is an honour bestowed by the British monarch, a prestigious title awarded for service.

clue.text: Interred, urned perhaps?

definitions.meaning: buried, which is literally placed beneath the earth
the word urned is the result of crushing (grinding) the letters of the word under, so it is one example of what the answer describes

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as UNDER + GROUND, an instruction: grind up the letters of under and you can get URNED. The clue gives the result and asks for the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something buried has been put beneath the soil, below the surface of the earth.

clue.text: Helpful Heather is fire starter

parts.note: kind, as in obliging
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather is good at getting the fire going.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; here it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling is the small dry wood used to get a fire lit before larger logs are added.

clue.text: Cover up aim to embrace quiet libertine lacking energy

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man

explanation.surface: A plan to hush up a scandal involving a worn-out rake.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshroud is to wrap or conceal completely, as if in a burial cloth.

clue.text: American opportunely heads for high yields, displaying coolness

parts.note: pat as an adverb means at just the right moment

indicators.note: only the leading letters of these two words are taken

parts.note: the two words each give their first letter

explanation.surface: A US investor shrugs at timely high returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or enthusiasm, an emotional coolness towards things.

clue.text: Cheat and solve this clue, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to do someone down is to swindle them
second meaning: this is a down clue, and to solve it is to do it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is self-referential: the clue sits in the down list, so doing it means doing a down.
explanation.definitionFit: To do down is a British idiom for getting the better of someone unfairly or belittling them.

clue.text: Oddly missing sign on hotel

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters drop out, leaving the second, fourth and sixth

its first letter drops out, continuing the run of odd letters missing

explanation.surface: Something has gone strangely missing from the board outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a small hotel or pub offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Trap agreed following call

indicators.note: the agreement word comes after the call

parts.note: ho is a shout to attract attention
OK means agreed

explanation.surface: A snare is accepted after a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is used to catch fish, and figuratively anything that snares someone is a trap.

clue.text: Individuals invading country forming another

definitions.note: short for another country, since the wordplay builds one country from a different one

indicators.note: the individuals get inside the borders of the country

parts.note: India
ones, as single people

explanation.surface: A band of people invades a land and founds a new nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word another: putting the individuals inside India forms a different country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation separate from India, a further country in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Musical performance around November 5th in calendar? Beats me

indicators.note: the duo goes round the other two letters

parts.note: a duo is a piece for two performers

indicators.note: take only the fifth letter of the word calendar

parts.note: its fifth letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: A recital around Bonfire Night, the fifth of November in the diary, baffles me.
explanation.walkthrough: November 5th looks like a date (Guy Fawkes Night in Britain); it splits into November and 5th in calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunno is a casual spoken form of I don't know, the same shrug as beats me.

clue.text: Caught someone gathering flock to fix back of wool jumper

indicators.note: the wool letter is fastened inside the herder
caught as in heard, so what follows is a sound-alike

parts.note: a herder rounds up animals

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word wool

parts.note: its last letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: A shepherd is heard mending the back of a woolly pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper means a sweater in Britain, which suits the wool; here it is an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler is an athlete who leaps over barriers in a race.

clue.text: Doctor Who hands over Rose finally — big mistake

parts.note: left and right, the two hands

indicators.note: only the last letter of Rose

parts.note: its last letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: The Doctor hands his companion Rose something, a TV moment gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who and Rose (Tyler, his companion) form the TV picture; Doctor is really the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring, often laughable blunder.

clue.text: The setter's popular, cheering about mobster's icing

indicators.note: the cheering word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: elating means making happy
the setter is I, so the setter's is I'm
in, as in fashionable

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being well liked and enjoying a gangster's cake decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliminating someone is a euphemism for killing them, the mob sense of icing.

clue.text: Dabbler — translated title accepted by Italian author

indicators.note: the poet's name takes the rearranged word into itself

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: translated suggests changing form, so the letters of title are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An amateur's rendering of a title is taken up by an Italian writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without serious commitment.

clue.text: Managed to interrupt Tory leader once making aggressive speech

indicators.note: the managed word breaks into the middle of the name

parts.note: William Hague led the Conservative (Tory) Party from 1997 to 2001
ran, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone breaks in on a former Conservative chief during a hostile address.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, ranting, forceful address to an audience.

clue.text: New Zealander Kelvin takes wicket in two

indicators.note: the wicket letter sits inside the two

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A New Zealand cricketer called Kelvin takes a wicket in two balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the friendly nickname for a person from New Zealand, after its national bird.

clue.text: Perhaps Berlin fertiliser manufacturer is short of time

definitions.note: Irving Berlin is an example of the answer

indicators.note: the manufacturer lacks the letter for time

parts.note: a composter turns waste into compost

explanation.surface: A German city's fertiliser firm is running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin looks like the German capital; it is the songwriter Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote songs such as White Christmas, an example of a music writer.

clue.text: Soldier with no idea, losing heart in irrational fear

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
taken as written

indicators.note: the word idea drops its two middle letters

parts.note: taken as written before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: A clueless trooper, faint-hearted, is gripped by panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoia is an unfounded suspicion that others are out to harm you, a baseless dread.

clue.text: Discovered nova, universal medium for source of life

indicators.note: dis-covered, with its covering (outer letters) removed

parts.note: taken as written before its outer letters are removed
U is the film certificate for universal
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: An astronomer finds a new star in a universal medium that seeds life.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered reads as found; split it as dis-covered, stripping the word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovum is an egg cell, from which a new organism develops.

clue.text: Apt to change look when removing current hat

parts.note: voilà, there it is, look
I is the physics symbol for electric current
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A fickle look appears once someone takes off a live hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes something liable to shift suddenly and unpredictably, unstable.

clue.text: Right time, when leaderless, for moderation

indicators.note: the time word loses its first letter

parts.note: a season is a period of time

explanation.surface: The right moment, without a leader, calls for restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason means sensible limits, as in within reason, so it fits moderation.

clue.text: Draft review of shambolic nephew's housing

indicators.note: re-viewed, so read backwards
the two words hold the letters inside them

parts.note: the end of shambolic and the start of nephew's hold the letters

explanation.surface: A sketch reviewing a messy nephew's living arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil something is to write it in provisionally, as a draft.

clue.text: Stick poster in this place

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement such as a poster
here

explanation.surface: Put up a bill right here, as if instructing a bill-sticker.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fixed to a surface, as glue does.

clue.text: Rustic in Nice left out

parts.note: pleasant, agreeable

explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the city on the French Riviera; it is the adjective nice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country person, a farm labourer of humble rural origins.

clue.text: Breathed hard in ear: raunchy or sad?

definitions.note: two senses of one colour word, both offered as the definition

indicators.note: what the listener hears, so a sound-alike

parts.note: blew, as in panted

explanation.definitionFit: Blue means both risqué (a blue joke) and depressed (feeling blue).

clue.text: Share American plant

parts.note: a lot is a portion or allotted share
US

explanation.surface: Splitting an American factory between owners.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a factory; it is the water lily.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic flowering species, sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Digit: it's one occasionally

the run of every other letter continues across the gap

explanation.surface: A number that crops up only now and again.

clue.text: Security guard swore at cinema chain in audition

explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a big British cinema chain; 'cussed Odeon' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper or caretaker charged with protecting a place, as a security guard does.

clue.text: Threesome in rude relations tangle messily rejecting ordered duos

indicators.note: messily says the letters of the fodder words are jumbled into a new arrangement
rejecting says some letters are thrown out of the jumble, and ordered says those thrown-out letters need not keep their printed sequence

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
the letters thrown out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A three-way affair among badly behaved relatives ends in a messy muddle, with the couples turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool the letters of RUDE RELATIONS TANGLE, take out D, U, O and S (the letters of 'duos'), and rearrange the remaining fifteen into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a lasting romantic entanglement of three people, a threesome in the emotional sense.
